name: Finland
tagline: Your IB grades alone can win a place — no entrance exam
summary: Finland is the one country on this list where your IB transcript is converted into a published, field-by-field points table and used to admit you directly. It is called todistusvalinta, certificate-based selection, and it means you can skip the SAT and skip entrance exams at most universities. The main door is a single joint application at Studyinfo, open 7-21 January 2027 for degrees starting in August 2027, with up to six ranked choices. As a Danish citizen you pay no tuition at all, in any language of instruction.
whyConsider: No tuition for EU/EEA citizens, including every English-taught bachelor's degree. A Danish student pays nothing.
Published IB points tables. You can look up exactly what a 6 in HL Maths is worth before you apply, instead of guessing.
Finland counts as a Nordic country for Danish SU, so support covers the whole programme plus up to twelve extra months rather than being capped at four years.
LUT runs non-competitive rolling admission from 1 September 2026 to 30 April 2027 — meet the published criteria and you are in, with no January scramble.
As a Nordic citizen you skip Migri entirely and just register your details with the population agency (dvv.fi).
watchOuts: The joint application window for autumn 2027 is 7-21 January 2027 — you apply fifteen months before you start, on predicted grades. Aalto's own page says 7-22 January, one day out from everyone else; check it nearer the time.
Helsinki is the exception: the IB route there is Admission Group 2, running 9-23 March 2027, not January. Åbo Akademi's bachelor application is also 9-23 March.
Several famous names have almost nothing in English at bachelor level: Helsinki has two programmes, Turku two, Vaasa one, and Åbo Akademi teaches every single bachelor's degree in Swedish.

Finnish medicine is taught in Finnish and uses a national entrance exam. No English-taught Finnish medicine bachelor's could be verified, and the health sciences points table may not cover medicine at all.
Institutional scholarships exist only for fee-paying non-EU students. If you pay no tuition there is nothing to waive, and Finland has no government scholarship scheme.
Housing in Helsinki is the real bottleneck. HOAS says waiting times run from a few weeks to over a year — apply the day your offer lands.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No single national minimum. LUT publishes the clearest floor: 24 or more total points plus the award of the Diploma. Other institutions set thresholds per subject rather than per total.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Thresholds are set on individual subject grades, not on HL/SL status. For engineering via certificate-based selection you need at least grade 2 in advanced mathematics and in chemistry or physics, with at least one of those at grade 4. For business you need only grade 2 in mathematics, advanced or basic. LUT requires HL Maths 4 for technology programmes, and SL Maths 5 or HL Maths 4 plus one humanities or science subject at 5 for business. LUT's accepted maths list does not include Applications and Interpretation SL.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: IB grades 7 down to 2 are given direct point values; there is no conversion to Finnish letter grades for scoring. Universities score five subjects with a field-specific maximum: Technology and Engineering 172.1, Economics/Liberal Arts/Natural Sciences 158.9, Health Sciences 155.6, Business 149.9. HL Maths at grade 7 is worth 39.7 in the engineering table against 28.2 for SL. Universities of applied sciences use a separate 198-point table over five subjects, where HL Maths 7 is worth 46 and SL Maths 7 is worth 40.
notes: The IB and the European Baccalaureate are the only foreign certificates that count for certificate-based selection wherever they were taken. German Reifeprüfung and DIA only count if completed in Finland. Oulu states in plain English that an IB Diploma earned abroad qualifies.
The Diploma must come from an accredited IB school. A foreign school-leaving certificate that is not an IB Diploma does not count.
If you did not take a subject that a table scores, you get zero for that slot but can still be admitted on the rest. You can only score each subject once — advanced or basic maths, not both.
Tampere lets IB holders apply in both admission groups I and II in the same January application, which is effectively two shots at a place.

The university scoring tables published for 2026 entry are the ones quoted here. The 2027 versions had not been published when this was researched, and the UAS 198-point table is labelled as applying to the 2026 rounds only. Recheck both in late 2026.
The Administrative and Social Sciences table and the Education table were not read. Whether the Health Sciences table covers medicine and dentistry is unverified.

deadlines.label: Joint application, English-taught bachelor's, autumn 2027 start
deadlines.notes: One form, maximum six programme choices. Confirmed for 2027 by Jyväskylä, Tampere, Oulu, Turku, Metropolia, TAMK, Arcada and Haaga-Helia. Aalto's page says 7-22 January, which contradicts every other source.

deadlines.label: University of Helsinki, Admission Group 2 (the IB route)
deadlines.notes: Helsinki splits its rounds: Group 1 on SAT/ACT runs 5-19 January 2027, and the certificate-based Group 2 runs two months later. Åbo Akademi's bachelor application is also 9-23 March 2027.

deadlines.label: Attachments and English-proficiency documents
deadlines.notes: Jyväskylä's attachment deadline, and also the deadline for English-proficiency proof and individual arrangements for the International UAS Exam.

deadlines.label: International UAS Exam
deadlines.notes: Taken remotely on your own computer from 12:00 Finnish time, proctored by SMOWL. Pre-identification 10-12 March, invitations by 22 March, results by 14 April 2027.

deadlines.label: Predicted IB grades to Studyinfo
deadlines.notes: Jyväskylä's published 2027 date. Turku's 2026 equivalent was 31 March; its 2027 date was not published when this was researched.

deadlines.label: LUT rolling admission window
deadlines.notes: Non-competitive. LUT states that if you meet all requirements you are admitted without competition while places last.

deadlines.label: Results published
deadlines.notes: Aalto Round A by 31 March 2027, Round B by 28 May 2027. Jyväskylä's certificate-based result for Business Innovation and Sustainability by 28 May 2027.

deadlines.label: Official final IB grades
deadlines.notes: Jyväskylä's published date, comfortably after IB results are released in early July.

steps: During autumn 2026, look up the certificate-based scoring table for your field at yliopistovalinnat.fi and work out what your predicted grades are actually worth. This is the step most applicants skip.

Check each shortlisted programme for which route it uses — certificate-based, SAT/ACT, the International UAS Exam, or a portfolio and interview. It varies programme by programme even inside one university.
Submit one Studyinfo form between 7 and 21 January 2027 with up to six choices in order of preference. Add Helsinki separately in March if you want it.
Upload your attachments and predicted grades by the stated deadline — 28 January 2027 at Jyväskylä, 1 April 2027 for predicted grades.
If any of your choices needs the International UAS Exam, register, do the pre-identification on 10-12 March and sit the exam remotely on 23 March 2027.
Accept your place when results arrive, then apply for student housing the same day.
After you arrive, register your personal details with the Digital and Population Data Services Agency at dvv.fi. As a Nordic citizen you do not deal with Migri at all.
application.selectionNotes: There is no single joint entrance exam for university bachelor's programmes in English. Universities run parallel admission groups: one ranked on SAT or ACT, one ranked on your certificate. Holding the IB usually exempts you from the SAT entirely — Oulu and Turku both say so directly. Universities of applied sciences use either the certificate route or the remote International UAS Exam, and a few also take the SAT. Aalto's Design and Media programme ignores academic grades altogether and decides on portfolio plus interview.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Studyinfinland advertises around 600 English-taught programmes, but that figure combines bachelor's and master's and is not broken down. The ten research universities together offer roughly 40-50 English-taught bachelor's degrees; the universities of applied sciences carry most of the volume. LUT alone teaches all 15 of its bachelor's degrees in English.
language.englishProof: Sitting the IB in English generally counts as proof. LUT states this most clearly: complete the IB in English and no further evidence is needed, or use English A1 at grade 2, English A2 at grade 5, English A literature or language and performance at grade 2, or English B at grade 5. Jyväskylä requires everyone including native speakers to prove English skills but accepts IB English as proof. Applying through the SAT route at a university of applied sciences removes the language requirement altogether.
notes: Finnish and Swedish-taught degrees are free to everyone regardless of nationality, but they are not realistic for a Danish school leaver.
Åbo Akademi teaches every bachelor's degree in Swedish and requires documented Swedish. A Danish student's Swedish may in practice be good enough — worth asking them directly.
TAMK asks for IELTS Academic 6.0. Its page also lists 'TOEFL iBT 35+', which looks like a section minimum rather than a total; do not rely on it without checking.
Metropolia's scholarships are conditional on learning Finnish, rising from 1,000 euros in year one to 3,000 euros in year three for a B1 YKI certificate.

tuitionEuEea.value: None. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay no tuition for a bachelor's degree in Finland, in any language of instruction.

tuitionNonEu.value: Roughly 8,000-20,000 euros per year nationally, with a statutory minimum of 1,500 euros. Verified examples: Metropolia 11,500 euros (12,000 for game art, game design, XR design and sustainable fashion) explicitly for study rights starting after 31 July 2027; LUT 12,000, or 10,000 in year one with a 2,000-euro early-bird discount; Haaga-Helia 11,000; LAB 11,000 or 9,000 if paid within three weeks; Arcada 9,800 from autumn 2026; Laurea 9,500; Vaasa 10,000; TAMK 12,000 with no intake year stated.

costs.applicationFee: 100 euros, but only for applicants who are not EU/EEA/Swiss citizens. A Danish student pays nothing.

livingCostMonthly.value: 900-1,200 euros per month depending on the city. The statutory minimum for a non-EU student residence permit is 800 euros a month, or 9,600 euros in the bank at application.

notes: Student union membership costs about 50-70 euros per academic year.
The student healthcare fee is 35.35 euros per term, 70.70 euros per year at the 2026 rate. Kela does not send a bill — you have to pay it yourself, by 15 March and 15 November.
A single room in a shared flat typically costs 200-380 euros per month nationally. HOAS studios in the Helsinki region were listed at 287-373 euros.

A claim that Finland is moving to full cost recovery or raising fees from 2026 could not be confirmed on any official source and is not stated here as fact. The evidence points both ways: Metropolia has already priced the post-July-2027 cohort upward while Arcada cut its fee for autumn 2026.

funding: Danish SU for a full degree abroad. Because Finland is a Nordic country, SU covers the prescribed length of the programme plus up to twelve extra months if you need them, rather than the four-year cap that applies elsewhere. You must be a Danish citizen, or an EU/EEA citizen who can document sufficient ties to Denmark, and the programme must be officially recognised in Finland. Apply in minSU Fast Track no later than the first month you want support for.

Kela, the Finnish social insurance agency, is effectively closed to you. It treats an EU/EEA student's stay as temporary regardless of how long the degree is. The one way in is work: ten hours a week or more for at least four months opens access to Finnish student financial aid during the working period.
Finland has no government scholarship scheme. Studyinfinland says so outright and warns that advertisements for 'fully funded Finland government scholarships' contain false information.

Institutional scholarships are tuition waivers for fee-paying non-EU students only. Verified waivers run from about 15 percent (Laurea) to 50 percent of the second instalment in year one (TAMK). If you pay no tuition, none of them apply to you.
workRights: EU/EEA citizens have full access to the Finnish labour market with no cap. Non-EU students on a study permit may work an average of 30 hours a week, which Migri expresses as 120 hours a month or 1,560 hours a year. Internships required by your degree do not count toward the limit.
residency: As a Danish citizen you do not apply to Migri and you do not need a residence permit. You register your personal data with the Digital and Population Data Services Agency at dvv.fi. This is simpler than the standard EU registration that other EU citizens have to do, and it is the correct route for anyone from Denmark, Iceland, Norway or Sweden. Non-EU students need a continuous type A residence permit for studies over 90 days, granted for the whole degree: 600 euros electronically, 750 on paper, or 400 and 430 for minors.
housing: Student housing is run by non-profit foundations, city by city: HOAS in the Helsinki region, TOAS in Tampere, and others elsewhere. You apply once you have been accepted. HOAS states plainly that waiting times run from a few weeks to over a year, which makes Helsinki the riskiest city to arrive in for an August start. Because certificate-based results can land as late as 28 May, you may have only three months to sort it out. Apply the day your offer arrives, and have a backup.
healthcare: Bring your Danish EHIC, the blue EU card. Degree students at universities and universities of applied sciences are also covered by FSHS/YTHS, the Finnish Student Health Service, provided you are registered as attending for the current semester. There is a contradiction worth resolving before you rely on it: Kela says every registered degree student pays the 70.70-euro annual healthcare fee, while the FSHS page says EU/EEA students with a valid insurance card are exempt. Ask FSHS directly.

institutions.name: University of Helsinki
institutions.englishBachelors: 2 — Liberal Arts and Sciences, and Science
institutions.note: Finland's only regular global top-100 university, but only two of its bachelor's degrees are in English. As an IB candidate you apply in the March group, 9-23 March 2027, not the January one — which at least means it does not clash with everything else.

institutions.name: Aalto University
institutions.englishBachelors: 6 programmes presented as 11 application options, including Design and Media, Economics, Finance, International Business, Computer Engineering, Data Science and Quantum Technology. Aalto's own page contradicts itself on the count.
institutions.note: The one place where raw IB grades alone can win an engineering or business seat with no SAT. For Design and Media, though, your IB score is irrelevant — a portfolio and interview decide it. Aalto's programme-level IB thresholds could not be read.

institutions.name: Tampere University
institutions.englishBachelors: 11 — including Automation and Robotics, Biomedical Engineering, Engineering Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science, Environmental Engineering and three Sustainable Urban Development tracks
institutions.note: The clearest two-bites option in Finland: holding the IB lets you apply in both admission group I and group II on the same January form. Eleven English-taught bachelor's degrees is among the widest choice at a Finnish research university.

institutions.name: LUT University
institutions.englishBachelors: 15 — every bachelor's degree LUT offers is taught in English, 13 in technology and 2 in business
institutions.note: The best-documented Finnish option for an IB student: a published 24-point floor, a named list of acceptable IB maths courses, and non-competitive rolling admission from 1 September 2026 to 30 April 2027. Meet the criteria and you are in, with no January deadline pile-up. Note that Maths AI SL is not on its accepted list.

institutions.name: University of Oulu
institutions.englishBachelors: 4 — Computer Science and Engineering, Electronics and Communications Engineering, Software Engineering and Information Systems, International Business Management, all 3+2
institutions.note: Home of the 6G Flagship programme. It also has the most IB-friendly wording of any Finnish university: it states in plain English that an IB Diploma earned abroad qualifies for certificate-based selection, which exempts you from the SAT.

institutions.name: University of Turku
institutions.englishBachelors: 2 — Sustainable and Social Entrepreneurship, and Information and Communication Technology (a combined 3+2). The count is uncertain because of how the ICT degree is listed.
institutions.note: Home of the Finland Futures Research Centre and one of the few places in Europe where futures studies is a real discipline. Holding the IB exempts you from the SAT for the ICT degree, but predicted grades go in by the end of March, so talk to your coordinator early.

institutions.name: University of Jyväskylä
institutions.englishBachelors: 3 — Business Innovation and Sustainability, Immersive Software Engineering and Artificial Intelligence, Early Childhood Education
institutions.note: Finland's original teacher-training seminary, which is why it dates to 1863 and why education is still its strongest field. It has already published firm 2027 dates — predicted grades 1 April, final grades 13 July — which is more than most institutions have done.

institutions.name: Åbo Akademi University
institutions.englishBachelors: None. Every bachelor's degree at Åbo Akademi is taught in Swedish and requires documented Swedish. Around 16 master's degrees are in English.
institutions.note: Finland's Swedish-language university, and closed to you at bachelor level unless you can read and write Swedish — though as a Dane your Swedish may be closer to adequate than most applicants', so it is worth asking. Its master's degrees in international law and human rights and in peace mediation are among the most distinctive in Europe. Åbo Akademi does not mention the IB anywhere on its English bachelor pages.

institutions.name: University of Eastern Finland
institutions.note: A large university formed by merging the Joensuu and Kuopio universities, with around 17,600 students. Its website blocked every attempt to read it, so nothing about its programmes, deadlines or IB handling could be verified — you will need to open it in a browser yourself. One thing that is worth knowing: the two campuses are 130 km apart, so check which city your programme is actually in.

institutions.name: Metropolia University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: 32 listed for the January 2027 cycle, but that count includes top-up degrees that require a prior qualification and duplicate delivery modes. The number genuinely open to a school leaver is lower.
institutions.note: Finland's widest English-taught offer at a university of applied sciences, and unusual for having creative degrees like game design and XR design in English. It appears on the official lists for both the International UAS Exam and certificate-based selection, so check which route your specific programme uses.

institutions.name: Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: 8 — Aviation Business, Business Information Technology, Digital Business Innovations, International Business, three hospitality and tourism degrees, and Sports Coaching and Management. All 210 ECTS over about 3.5 years.
institutions.note: The clearest non-exam route among the universities of applied sciences: certificate-based or SAT, with rolling admission from 30 October 2026 to 12 May 2027, so you never have to sit the International UAS Exam.

institutions.name: Tampere University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: 10 — including Environmental Engineering and Green Transition, Software Engineering, Textile and Material Engineering, Media and Arts, International Business and Team Entrepreneurship
institutions.note: The most transparent of the universities of applied sciences about which admission route applies to which programme. It accepts the SAT for three named engineering and software degrees, deadline 31 March 2027, and uses certificate-based selection for Media and Arts and Team Entrepreneurship.

institutions.name: Laurea University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: 7 — Nursing, Social Services, Service Experience Management, Safety Security and Risk Management, Business Management, Cyber Security, Developing Digital Services. All 210 ECTS over 3.5 years.
institutions.note: The Safety, Security and Risk Management degree is close to unique in English anywhere in the EU, and worth a look if criminology or security work interests you. Laurea's 2027 dates and selection methods could not be verified — its criteria page was not reachable.

institutions.name: Arcada University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: 4 — Information Technology (Engineering), International Business, Mechanical and Sustainable Engineering, and a Nursing top-up. The listing read was for the 2026 intake.
institutions.note: Small, Swedish-speaking and right in central Helsinki, which makes it an unusually easy cultural landing for a Dane. It names the IB explicitly in its eligibility rules, but some of that wording ties qualifications to completion in Finland — confirm your route before January 2027.
